threads.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse colon-led table delimiters**

When a list-item continuation is `- Context.\n  :-`, `micromark` renders `:-` as the delimiter of a one-column GFM table, but this new allowlist admits the leading colon while `opensTable` only detects headers containing a pipe. Consequently, `ground --check` reports no `unmodelled-construct` and extracts the single prose unit `Context. :-` even though the reader sees a table, allowing the table contents to be grounded as unrelated prose. Either recognize this delimiter shape or remove `:` from the continuation allowlist.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L305-L312](https://github.com/rookslog/stylewright/blob/47be915cc8360e917dd9bb6a27d164263b0cc96f/AGENTS.md#L305-L312)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

replies.author: rookslog
replies.body:
```review-verdict
verdict: ACCEPTED_MODIFIED
commit: 229c58f
finding_category: content-escape
reviewer: chatgpt-codex-connector
```

Confirmed against the render, and the class is wider than the shape reported.
Both suggested exits were declined for the same reason: each closes one shape
and leaves the rest.

Neither `recognize this delimiter shape` nor `remove : from the continuation
allowlist` is what landed. Reading the table needs a second row-recognition
rule, because a one-column table has no pipe in its ROWS either, plus a
decision about where such a table ends, and it collides with the delimiter
cell-count divergence issue #117 already carries. Removing the colon closes
`- Context.` over `:-` and leaves six shapes at column 0 open, which never
reach the continuation form at all.

So the check refuses the shape, by ADR-0016's rule: a construct the walk cannot
model is named rather than read. One predicate, every indent.

`:-:`, `-:`, `:---:`, `-|` and `|-` are tables to both parsers and are refused
with it. `---`, `-` and `--` are setext underlines and are not, because a colon
or a pipe in the delimiter is the whole difference. A delimiter with no header
above it is no table to either reader.

Accounting: this is on `main` unchanged, and the column-0 half does not depend
on the continuation grammar at all.
